title: Property Management Software: Seven Tools Priced by Unit
html:
Property management software runs rent, leases, maintenance and accounting, and the right pick depends on how many units you manage. Landlords with a few doors can start free or near free, while firms with hundreds of units pay per unit. Pair the system with a website and steady lead generation so the units you manage keep growing. Published prices in this guide run from no monthly fee to $5.00 per unit a month.

Property management software has to do three jobs: collect rent, keep the books and track every repair. Most tools do all three, so price and limits decide the choice. This guide sorts seven tools by the size of portfolio each one fits, with the price each vendor publishes and one real limit for each.

Software only manages the units you already hold. Filling vacancies and winning new owners takes marketing.

Which property management software fits a growing portfolio?

AppFolio, Buildium and DoorLoop are the three most firms compare once they pass a few dozen units. They differ mainly in how they charge.

  • AppFolio: lists three plans, Core at $1.49 per unit a month, Plus at $3.20 and Max at $5.00, each labeled starting at. Limit: Core carries a 50-unit minimum and a minimum spend, and the page does not state the dollar amount of that minimum.
  • Buildium: lists Essential at $65 a month, Growth at $202 and Premium at $420, all as starting prices. Essential covers basic accounting, maintenance, leasing and communications. Limit: new customers on Growth or Premium must use Buildium's onboarding service, and the page states no unit minimums.
  • DoorLoop: lists DoorLoop One at $2.50 per unit a month, with rates as low as $1.50 per unit above 100 units. Connect is $4.00 and Multiply is $5.00 by invitation. Limit: each plan note says a minimum spend and unit count apply, so ask for the total before you commit.

Per-unit and flat pricing cross at a unit count you can calculate. Take 50 units. At the listed starting rates, AppFolio Core is 50 times $1.49, or $74.50, before the minimum spend. DoorLoop One is 50 times $2.50, or $125. Buildium Essential is a flat $65.

These figures are arithmetic from listed starting prices, not quotes. Minimums, add-ons and payment fees change the final bill. Ask each vendor for a written total at your exact unit count.

Which property management software is cheapest for a small landlord?

Innago and TenantCloud are the low-cost options in this guide. Both target owners with a small number of units who want rent collection and applications without an accounting team.

  • Innago: its published plans headline reads Simple, Powerful, Free, with no monthly fee, no setup fee and no contract. Limit: the page text does not list unit limits or payment processing fees, so check the vendor before you rely on it.
  • TenantCloud: lists Starter at $15 a month billed annually, Growth at $29 and Pro at $50, with a 14-day trial. Starter includes online rent payments, maintenance, listings and applications for unlimited properties. Limit: Starter caps at 10 leases and excludes the owner portal, and the page shows conflicting monthly prices, so check the vendor.

Small landlords also change tools more often than large firms, so avoid long contracts. Innago lists no contract, and TenantCloud lists a 14-day trial on each plan. A trial that needs no migration work is the cheapest way to learn whether a tool fits how you collect rent.

Free and low-cost tools earn their place until the lease count rises. TenantCloud's 10-lease cap is a clear trigger. When you pass it, you either upgrade or move to a per-unit platform.

Plan the move before you need it. Export tenant and ledger data once a quarter, so a switch is a few hours of work instead of a month of rebuilding records.

Which website tool helps a property management firm get found?

A property management firm needs a website that owners can read and renters can search. Wix lets a small firm launch one without a developer.

  • Wix: a drag and drop builder with hosting and templates. The shows Light at $17.77 a month, Core at $29.77 and Business at $39.77, for yearly subscriptions paid in full. Limit: the page says prices and currency vary by location, and storage is 2 GB on Light.

A builder gives you the tool, not the traffic. Owners search for a manager by city and by service, so each market needs its own page.

Pair the site with an inquiry form that tells owners and renters apart. A single contact form buries owner leads under repair requests. Two forms, one for owners and one for renters, keep both lists clean.

Which free tool puts a property management company on the map?

Google Business Profile is the free listing that shows your firm in Google Maps and local search. Google states that you can add or claim your business at no charge.

  • Google Business Profile: shows your name, service area, photos, reviews and phone number when an owner searches for property management nearby. Limit: it needs current photos, posts and review replies, and it does not manage a single unit. See Google's Business Profile help page.

Reviews on that listing shape owner trust. For a harsh review, read how to answer a negative review first.

What does property management software cost at 25 and 100 units?

At 25 units a flat plan wins, and at 100 units a per-unit plan can win. The numbers below use only the starting prices listed on each vendor page.

  • 25 units: DoorLoop One is 25 times $2.50, or $62.50. Buildium Essential starts at a flat $65. AppFolio Core does not apply, because its page lists a 50-unit minimum.
  • 100 units: AppFolio Core is 100 times $1.49, or $149, before its minimum spend. DoorLoop One is 100 times $2.50, or $250. Buildium Essential still starts at $65, though its feature set is the smallest.
  • Where flat pricing stops: Buildium's page does not state unit minimums, so ask whether Essential covers your count. A cheap plan that cannot hold your units is not cheap.

Feature tiers matter as much as the unit math. Buildium Essential lists basic accounting, while Growth adds reporting automation and enhanced tenant screening. If you need owner reports with detail, price the tier that includes them.

Which fees sit behind the property management software price?

Payment, screening and signature fees often sit outside the plan price. Read the fee lines on every vendor page before you sign.

  • Payment processing: Innago's page text lists no processing fees, so ask for the ACH and card rates. Buildium lists first-year-free incoming EFT transactions on Premium, which implies a fee on other plans.
  • Tenant screening: TenantCloud lists full tenant screenings as free on all plans, with the cost paid by the applicant. Confirm who pays at every vendor.
  • Signatures and onboarding: Buildium lists lower-cost eSignatures on Growth, and requires its onboarding service for new Growth and Premium customers.
  • Texts and extras: TenantCloud Starter limits lead text messages to 10, so a busy leasing season can exhaust that quickly.

A fee that is small per transaction can be large per year. Estimate your monthly rent payments, applications and signatures, then multiply by the rate each vendor quotes.

What should you move from spreadsheets first?

Move rent roll and balances first, because every other report depends on them. Everything else can follow in the order below.

  • Week one: import units, tenants, leases and current balances. Check ten tenants by hand against the old sheet.
  • Week two: connect the bank account and post one full month of rent and expenses. Run one owner statement and compare totals.
  • Week three: turn on maintenance requests and tenant payments, and tell tenants where to log in.
  • Week four: archive the old sheet in read-only form and keep it for your records.

This order keeps risk low. A mistake in the rent roll shows up in week one, when it is cheap to fix. A mistake found at tax time is not.

How do you choose property management software?

Choose property management software with a three-check filter: fit, cost and setup effort. Run every tool through all three before you pay.

Fit: does it handle your unit count, your property types and your owner reporting? A single-family portfolio and a 200-unit complex need different features.

Cost: multiply per-unit prices by your units, then add minimum spend, onboarding, payment fees and extra users. Compare the total, not the headline.

Setup effort: can you import tenants, leases and balances in a week, or does the vendor charge for onboarding?

A landlord with a handful of doors can run Innago or TenantCloud Starter, plus a free Google Business Profile. A firm with a growing book of owners fits Buildium, AppFolio or DoorLoop, plus a managed website.

Test with real data. Load one building into a trial account, post one month of rent and run one owner statement. A tool that handles that cleanly will handle the rest.

What should property management software report to owners?

Property management software should give each owner a monthly statement showing rent collected, expenses paid and the net amount sent. Owners judge a manager by that page.

  • Rent roll: every unit, tenant, rent amount and balance in one view.
  • Owner statement: income, expenses and the payout, with receipts attached.
  • Maintenance log: each request, who fixed it and what it cost.
  • Vacancy list: which units are empty and how long they have been listed.

Before you buy, ask each vendor to show a sample owner statement. If the sample is hard to read, your owners will say so.

Reporting is also a sales tool. A clear statement is the page an owner shows a friend who is weighing a switch. Treat the report layout as part of the price you are paying, and test it with one real owner before you commit to a year.

How do you bring owners and renters to the software?

Software fills with units only when owners hand you buildings and renters apply for them. Both need marketing that points to a clear page.

Search ads from property management Google Ads and rankings from property management SEO send owners to your site.

What is the best property management software?

The best pick depends on your unit count and budget. Innago and TenantCloud suit small landlords, while AppFolio, Buildium and DoorLoop suit larger portfolios. Load one building into a trial and compare real totals.

How much does property management software cost?

Published prices in this guide run from no monthly fee for Innago to $5.00 per unit a month for AppFolio Max. Buildium Essential starts at $65 a month, and TenantCloud Starter lists at $15 a month on annual billing. Minimums and add-ons raise the total.

Is there free property management software?

Innago lists no monthly fee, no setup fee and no contract on its published plans. The page does not list unit limits or payment fees, so check the vendor. TenantCloud has no free plan listed, but offers a 14-day trial on every plan.

What does AppFolio cost per unit?

AppFolio lists Core at $1.49 per unit a month, Plus at $3.20 and Max at $5.00, each labeled starting at. Core has a 50-unit minimum and a minimum spend that the page does not price. Ask for a written quote at your unit count.

What should small landlords look for in property management software?

Look for online rent payments, maintenance requests, applications and a clear lease cap. TenantCloud Starter caps at 10 leases. Check payment processing fees, because pages may not list them. Make sure you can export your data in case you outgrow the tool.

Can property management software bring me new owners?

No. It manages the units you already hold. New owners come from a website, a Google Business Profile and advertising. Use the software for rent and records, and use marketing to find owners who want a manager for their buildings.

multiply per-unit prices by your units, then add minimum spend, onboarding, payment fees and extra users. Compare the total, not the headline.
Setup effort:
can you import tenants, leases and balances in a week, or does the vendor charge for onboarding?
A landlord with a handful of doors can run Innago or TenantCloud Starter, plus a free Google Business Profile. A firm with a growing book of owners fits Buildium, AppFolio or DoorLoop, plus a managed website.
Test with real data. Load one building into a trial account, post one month of rent and run one owner statement. A tool that handles that cleanly will handle the rest.
##
What should property management software report to owners?
Property management software should give each owner a monthly statement showing rent collected, expenses paid and the net amount sent. Owners judge a manager by that page.
-
Rent roll:
every unit, tenant, rent amount and balance in one view.
-
Owner statement:
income, expenses and the payout, with receipts attached.
-
Maintenance log:
each request, who fixed it and what it cost.
-
Vacancy list:
which units are empty and how long they have been listed.
Before you buy, ask each vendor to show a sample owner statement. If the sample is hard to read, your owners will say so.
Reporting is also a sales tool. A clear statement is the page an owner shows a friend who is weighing a switch. Treat the report layout as part of the price you are paying, and test it with one real owner before you commit to a year.
##
How do you bring owners and renters to the software?
Software fills with units only when owners hand you buildings and renters apply for them. Both need marketing that points to a clear page.
Search ads from property management Google Ads and rankings from property management SEO send owners to your site.
###
What is the best property management software?
The best pick depends on your unit count and budget. Innago and TenantCloud suit small landlords, while AppFolio, Buildium and DoorLoop suit larger portfolios. Load one building into a trial and compare real totals.
###
How much does property management software cost?
Published prices in this guide run from no monthly fee for Innago to $5.00 per unit a month for AppFolio Max. Buildium Essential starts at $65 a month, and TenantCloud Starter lists at $15 a month on annual billing. Minimums and add-ons raise the total.
###
Is there free property management software?
Innago lists no monthly fee, no setup fee and no contract on its published plans. The page does not list unit limits or payment fees, so check the vendor. TenantCloud has no free plan listed, but offers a 14-day trial on every plan.
###
What does AppFolio cost per unit?
AppFolio lists Core at $1.49 per unit a month, Plus at $3.20 and Max at $5.00, each labeled starting at. Core has a 50-unit minimum and a minimum spend that the page does not price. Ask for a written quote at your unit count.
###
What should small landlords look for in property management software?
Look for online rent payments, maintenance requests, applications and a clear lease cap. TenantCloud Starter caps at 10 leases. Check payment processing fees, because pages may not list them. Make sure you can export your data in case you outgrow the tool.
###
Can property management software bring me new owners?
No. It manages the units you already hold. New owners come from a website, a Google Business Profile and advertising. Use the software for rent and records, and use marketing to find owners who want a manager for their buildings.
